title: How AI Learns: Training a Neural Network in 60 Seconds 🧠 #shorts
description:
A neural network starts out knowing nothing. Training is a loop: make a guess (forward pass), measure how wrong it is (the loss), work out which weights caused the error (backpropagation) and nudge each one a tiny step downhill (gradient descent). Repeat millions of times and the loss falls until the guesses are right.

lines: Every AI model starts out completely clueless. Its first guesses are pure noise.
Step one: guess. The input flows through layers of neurons, each one multiplying by a weight, and out comes a prediction.
Step two: measure the mistake. The loss is a single number that says how wrong that guess was.
Step three: blame. Backpropagation works backwards and finds how much each weight caused the error.
Step four: nudge. Every weight moves a tiny step downhill, so next time the loss is a little lower.
Repeat that loop millions of times, and the guesses go from noise to right.
Guess. Measure. Blame. Nudge. That's how AI learns.
